I took my cat to the dentist and it was decided to start gnawing on the anal glands. This led to the cat licking its anus and the whole area becoming inflamed. We had to go to the emergency room over the weekend, the cat was given a bunch of medications and a cone on its head for a week. We discussed the matter with the doctor at Lexavet and his opinion was that if there had been no problems with the glands before, then there would be soon. They have a standard for keeping a thermometer in the anus during dental care and that's when they noticed that the glands were full. The cat is 15 years old and has never had any problems before. I find it strange that I would take my cat to the dentist and there they would "treat" something that might start to bother me in the future or not. The dental care already cost 1200 e, so I didn't really want to pay for an emergency room visit, new medications and, least of all, watch for a week while the cat was mentally dead because of the cone.
I want to be able to trust the vet, but in this case, the trust in the position was lost, so we will move on elsewhere.

At Lexavet, both pets and people are warmly welcomed. The staff, who are clearly knowledgeable in their field, seem to remember and take into account each animal and its situation individually. No attempt is made to "squeeze" procedures or follow-up visits into the clinic in order to collect financial profits, but rather they are weighed up and the treatment plan is discussed openly in advance with the client. My sensitive, easily frightened, rescue-backed cat has received the most gentle care, and the in-house veterinarian, who is familiar with feline medicine and specializes in internal diseases, has been a great part of the team for us. Appointments and communication are handled quickly, clearly and smoothly, appointments have often been found quickly, and the opening hours are suitably extensive. It is also easy to get to the veterinary clinic by public transport. Lexavet has been a perfect find for us. 🩷
